chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about scattered sweets of sugar, almonds, and the like—whether eating them is permissible. He said: “Anything seized by snatching is disliked.”

key_terms.أَشْبَاهِهِ: similar items of the same kind
key_terms.النُّثَارِ: scattered sweets or items thrown out for people to pick up
key_terms.يُنْتَهَبُ: is seized by snatching or plundered

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat scattered sweets or gifts taken by snatching?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on eating treats scattered among people when they are taken through scrambling and snatching. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that wealth taken in such a manner is disliked, indicating disapproval of consuming property acquired through wrongful seizure.
